text:
Let me start by asking: When did this rear-end collision occur, and was there any immediate loss of consciousness or memory loss around the time of impact? Additionally, can you describe exactly how your right leg was positioned when you were first seen after the accident?

REQUEST TEST: CT_Spine

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Hip Dislocation.

The classic presentation of a shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated leg following a rear-end collision is pathognomonic for this injury. The CT_Spine results are secondary; an immediate Orthopedic Consultation for closed reduction is required.
